name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social media, including the CooRnet methodology and its successor VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution, actively extended through 2026 with new alert systems and encyclopedia/handbook chapters.

name: Platform Data Governance & Access
description: Research on the shifting infrastructure of platform data access for scholars (CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta URL Shares Dataset, DSA-mandated researcher APIs) and on platform content-moderation policies such as Meta's political content reduction and its effects on political actors' visibility.

name: Disinformation Narrative Monitoring
description: Development of monitoring dashboards, language models and educational resources to track evolving disinformation narratives in Europe (war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, elections), centered on the PROMPT project and related fact-checker support tools.

name: Generative AI and Media Manipulation
description: Study of how generative AI is used in deceptive information operations and coordinated promotional campaigns (e.g., AI-generated imagery in gambling ads, iterative deception tactics), plus critical/pedagogical work on generative AI and media, reflecting a fast-growing 2025–2026 strand and a new taught course.

name: LLM-Assisted Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on integrating large language models into content analysis and annotation pipelines for political discourse and complex social phenomena, including validation challenges and comparative embedding-model studies, an active collaborative line with international AoIR working groups.

name: Political Polarization and Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan media ecosystems, affective engagement in partisan online communities, and the interplay between social and traditional media in amplifying political polarization, spanning Italian, Brazilian and comparative contexts.

name: Electoral Social Media Research
description: Country-specific studies of social media dynamics around elections (Italy 2018/2022, Germany 2021, Brazil post-Bolsonaro), examining coordinated networks, political advertising and hyperpartisan pages during campaigns — the empirical backbone of the MINE programme.

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Mapping of coordinated networks circulating problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration tools and country studies in India and Nigeria funded by the Gates Foundation.

name: MINE — Mapping Italian News Program
description: The institutional umbrella research programme, founded in 2017 and still active, investigating Italian media coverage and social media's impact on elections, public opinion and health information; it has hosted the majority of the researcher's funded sub-projects.

name: Information Disorder Theory
description: Conceptual and taxonomic work on misinformation, 'fake news' and coordination/inauthenticity within the hybrid media system, providing the theoretical grounding cited across handbook and encyclopedia entries and underpinning applied detection work.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
